scope: FD198 reservation before opening streams; owned close and child cleanup
Final parent plus reaped children CPU and wall accounting
observations: The private trace descriptor is checked vacant, reserved with an owned /dev/null mapping before any of the four streams opens, and explicitly excluded from all four stream descriptors before duplication. Thus a stream cannot accidentally acquire 198 between the vacancy check and duplication in this single-threaded capture.

Owned descriptor state is consumed before close. Close exceptions are collected; independent kill and a finally wait attempt still execute. The changed control flow repairs the two previously identified source-level gaps. This was not an executed fault reproduction.

Both finalizers perform source/image after-checks before the final aggregate CPU/wall measurement. A mismatch, aggregate CPU >=90 or elapsed >=180 seconds forces FAIL. Existing per-child limits and complete calibration comparisons are unchanged.

The timing capture remains diagnostic: same 63 semantic images, two calibration processes and one actual large input process. Timing hooks/layout overhead are not hidden or counted as an original semantic qualification.
failure_evidence_scope: cleanup-errors.json is written after child cleanup. If that evidence write itself raises, it can mask a pre-existing primary exception; the child cleanup attempts have already occurred. No claim is made that all filesystem-write failures preserve the original exception object.
The review does not prove successful runtime FD behavior, timing observations, packer results, or a complete publication/CLI chain.
